STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, flat centre, no inner wall visible).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, medium-large, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the plate spans roughly 2.2 scrambled-egg-cluster widths... more usefully, the scrambled egg mound and the sweet potato pieces are each roughly 2-3 cm across. The plate width is about 9-10 of those pieces, giving roughly 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm (area 625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: covers roughly 22% of the plate, about 137 cm². Mound averages about 1.5 cm thick (peak about 3 cm). Volume = 137 x 1.5 = 206 ml. Density 0.8 g/ml gives about 165 g.
- Raspberries/blackberries: about 6% of the plate, about 38 cm², with a flat layer roughly 1 cm thick (berries stacked about 2 deep). Volume about 38 ml x 0.6 = 23 g for the fruit. Count is roughly 12 raspberries (about 5 g each) and 4 blackberries (about 6 g each), so about 60 g total. Use 60 g.
- Roasted sweet potato: about 15% of the plate, about 94 cm². Pieces are chunky, about 2 cm thick on average (peak around 3 cm). Volume = 94 x 2 = 188 ml. Density 0.6 gives about 113 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the egg and berries sit directly on the plate with no visible base layer, so no extra items are added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Scrambled egg (cooked with some fat): about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Mixed berries (raspberry/blackberry): about 50 kcal/100 g.
- Roasted sweet potato: about 110 kcal/100 g (with a little oil, roughly 120).

Totals: egg 165 g (about 248 kcal), berries 60 g (about 30 kcal), sweet potato 113 g (about 124 kcal). Overall roughly 338 kcal for about 340 g of food.
